lines: Status 194 · 2026-11-27 04:29 UTC · Phase 6

Decision needed from Brandon, unchanged, one thing only he can do: the automation that restarts this build ends Friday noon Mountain Time and a run may not move its own end. He can move the end to Sunday noon in the automation's settings, or write any line in the thread. The Partner raises it again Friday morning. Open item 252.

Chain 14 is read whole and on origin main (`fe261991`, pushed 04:23 UTC), one merge: the glass's outline loses its pale hairline in all four seasons. On it: tsc exit 0, build exit 0, engine `18322b0aa01a6cca`; the whole vitest 66 files passed and 1 skipped, 921 tests passed and 4 skipped; "pass M3 summer-rest: 0.9528"; "pass M3 spring-rest: 0.7655"; "FAIL M3 fall-rest: 0.7228 (threshold 0.75, detail.minSharpnessRatio)", the same failure as before, not made by this merge; M4 0.9694, 0.9049, 0.9546, 0.9602 and M5 0.993, 1, 0.969, 0.9997, all pass; all eight draft stills changed, and measured where: 3,950 to 5,098 pixels over 2 levels in each, all on the ball's outline, nothing inside the ball, on the base or on the table; triangles unchanged; `node tools/miniatures.mjs` pass. This closes the dotted outline among the 4K motion faults.

Chain 15 is being read on three merges that are not on origin main yet (local `d42a96a8`, started 04:24 UTC): summer's base fifth list, summer's sand fifth list first push, fall's base third list. Read so far: tsc exit 0; both makes exit 0 (fall's base 79,462 triangles); build exit 0, engine `204e27eb83ed197f`; "pass M3 summer-rest: 0.8467" (base 0.847; it was 0.9528 and falls because the grain on the sand was taken down as ordered; the picture is the aim, not the number); "pass M3 fall-rest: 0.797 (threshold 0.75, detail.minSharpnessRatio)". Still to come: the change's M4 and M5, the eight stills, the counts, the whole vitest.

Fall's line passes for the first time, and how it does is said plainly: its builder reports that most of the rise is relief in the surface drawn from a noise field (ridges on the bark, a pebbled hide), which the approved picture shows as form; without it the base stands near 0.72 (STATED). Ruled: such relief is allowed when it is fixed to the object and no bolder than the approved's; at 3840 the bark reads as rows of scales, so it is ordered finer. By eye fall's base is still below the bar.

Picture 1 is summer at rest as chain 15 drew it, approved picture left, build right. The sand of the base is smooth now and the speckle is gone. Below the bar: the base is browner and flatter than the approved's cream with its deep folds, the shells are grey brown where the approved's are cream white, the sea glass is dark, the cottage small and dark, the pond pale, the heap of sand a small wedge.

Picture 2 is fall at rest as chain 15 drew it, approved picture left, build right. New in the base: thick wound vines at the left in place of thirty thin twigs, five long thorns over the lip, a fuller web. Below the bar: the right flank is bare hide where the approved has thin black vines, the left vines are pale where the approved's are dark with copper lights, the left pumpkin's rind reads purple; and as before the leaves are too many and too large, the bats too large, the tree paler than the approved's.

Picture 3 is summer's base alone: the approved picture above, the fourth list in the middle, the fifth list below. The low left flank went from 119,80,42 to 132,90,47 against the approved's 168,115,57 (STATED by its builder). The sixth list is ordered: shells and sea glass first, then the depth of the folds, then a pale bar with a straight lower edge.

Picture 4 is summer's sand at 3840 by 2160 in film frame 1875, at one to one above and at five times below. Before, left: each lying grain is drawn as a three pronged shape or a row of beads. With the mend, right: one soft disc each. Its builder says plainly that the discs are very even in size, and that is ordered varied. In the same push the heap's shade turns from a hard blue grey triangle to a warm grey with a soft edge; the heap's size and the breadth of its shade are ordered next.

Winter's pond is closed by eye: on its mender's strip of film frames 29 to 32 at 3840 at eight times, with the camera's travel taken out, the dashes stand still on the ice and nothing in the lamp's light jumps; what moves is grain sized (2.4 to 2.6 levels) but for two or three dashes of a few pixels at the light's ragged left edge that neither of us can see move at one to one.

The page's carried state has its cause named and a mend on its builder's machine (STATED): one shared twinkle value of the miniature trees' lights was written by winter, summer and fall and read by spring, so a frame depended on what the page drew before it (film frame 690: 4,601 pixels by at most 1 level). Each season now gets its own. The proof is running: thirteen frames, each drawn first in a fresh page and again after the thirty frames before it, to be equal byte for byte; push by 05:25 UTC. No master frame is drawn before it is on main.

Summer's tree seventh pass has arrived (STATED): with the air the pair reads as one tree, without the air not yet (ours is the fuller crown, its lit tops dimmer); its M3 on the builder's machine is 0.7653, a margin of 0.015 over the line. I look at its eight pictures next and decide on the merge.

The next publish of the app: its 40 first pictures are being drawn on a helper machine on chain 15's tree since 04:28 UTC. The app is published once chain 15 is read whole and the checks and the security review pass, about 05:35 UTC.
14 agents were at work at 04:28 UTC.

Render counts since the last status. Drawn here: chain 14's change measure and eight draft stills; chain 15's two review stills so far. On helper machines: the builders' own stills and frames. No frame of the masters yet.
Sound: 7,420 of 10,000 credits, unchanged, no call planned.
